factor_diagnostics.value_notes: NOAA's California halibut SST assessment uses 12-20 °C as an egg-suitability threshold based on laboratory egg development; USGS experiments found eggs hatched at 12, 16 and 20 °C but not at 8 or 24 °C. Juvenile studies report preferred temperatures varying with acclimation (15.1-24.7 °C; final preferendum 18.4 °C). This supports thermal relevance, but egg and juvenile responses differ and do not establish a universal adult SST catch curve. The configured 12-21 °C / 14-19 °C bands remain provisional for mixed life stages.

factor_diagnostics.value_notes: NOAA's 2025 species synthesis reports mature California halibut in nearshore coastal waters to about 100 m, with most mature fish shallower than 30 m; juveniles rely on estuaries and embayments. This supports shallow demersal habitat but the configured 2-60 m band and 4-55 m ideal extend well beyond the depth range used by most mature fish and do not represent nursery habitat separately.
